Article Title: Another review on the cards? More changes likely in India's backroom staff after the Sri Lanka Tests
Article Text:
Team Doctor Rizwan Khan (left) and head physiotherapist Kamlesh Jain (Instagram)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the best way for a team to tackle frequent player injuries? Stricter fitness standards & longer recovery time Rotating players to manage workload 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is expected to assess the Indian team's injury concerns in the coming weeks. TimesofIndia.com has learnt that the current team management will provide feedback on physiotherapist Kamlesh Jain, who has been with the side since taking over from Nitin Patel in 2022. India have been grappling with injuries and frequent breakdowns in the past few months, and Jasprit is the latest addition to the growing list.Harshit Rana and Nitish Kumar Reddy were also unavailable for selection due to their respective injuries. Washington Sundar is out of the first Test and remains highly doubtful for the second. Sai Sudharsan has also been picked in the squad, subject to fitness clearance from the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE).Multiple discussions on the subject took place during the recent white-ball series in England, and both captain Shubman Gill and coach Gautam Gambhir are displeased with the frequent breakdowns. It has been a frustrating period for both the captain and coach, as they have been forced to play without their first-choice squad due to availability issues."It becomes a little difficult when you come to the ground in the morning and find out that a player has a niggle.Then it's almost like asking whether you want to take a chance. If a player is only 80% fit and you are playing with five bowlers, and that player comes off after bowling five overs, then who will bowl? This is difficult. So, as a group, we need to improve our fitness and all those things," Gill had said after the Lord's defeat last month.Many fingers have been pointed at the CoE over these frequent injury concerns, including at head physiotherapist Kamlesh. Many senior players are seeking opinions from specialists outside the BCCI setup, and some have even found the transition from former Strength and Conditioning Coach Soham Desai to Adrian Le Roux less than ideal."The role of head physio Kamlesh Jain is under the scanner, as is that of the experts at the CoE. These injury concerns aren't ideal because both the captain and coach have regularly struggled to field a full-strength Playing XI. How can one think about the right playing combination when even the 15 isn't their first choice?" questioned a source tracking developments."There is so much competition for each spot that a player is expected to push his body. This is where the support staff and the CoE need to step in. They need to raise the red flags and not rush players back into action. The situation is now becoming a bit embarrassing, and every concerned person needs to be held accountable.Was Nitish Reddy 100% fit when he played the third ODI against Afghanistan? Was Harshit rushed back? These are some very valid questions that require explanations," added the source.India are staring at a packed calendar, starting with the two Tests against Sri Lanka, and the end of that series could force the BCCI to explore different names for the positions of head physiotherapist and even team doctor. Kamlesh Jain and Dr Rizwan Khan currently occupy those two positions.
Article Summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is expected to assess the Indian team's injury concerns in the coming weeks. The current team management will provide feedback on physiotherapist Kamlesh Jain. India have been grappling with injuries and frequent breakdowns in the past few months.

Article Title: 'Today is a happy day': Brij Bhushan Singh's first reaction after acquittal in sexual harassment case
Article Text:
Brij Bhushan Singh (PTI Photo)

Delhi court acquits Brij Bhushan Singh and Vinod Tomar

Trial followed nationwide protests



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Monday welcomed the Delhi court's decision acquitting him in the sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers, describing it as a "happy day" for himself and his supporters while saying he would wait for the detailed judgment before commenting further.A Delhi court acquitted Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar in the high-profile case that had dominated Indian wrestling for more than two years and sparked nationwide protests by some of the country's top wrestlers.Speaking to reporters shortly after the verdict, Singh reiterated the stand he had maintained since the allegations first surfaced."On the first day, when my first statement came, I had said that if any verdict or any charge is proven, I will hang myself. Today, the court acquitted me with honour. It is a matter of joy for me and my supporters... Today is a happy day," Singh said.He also thanked his legal team for their efforts and said he would wait for the court's detailed order before making any further comments on the case.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwani Panwar of the Rouse Avenue Court pronounced the verdict, acquitting both Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar.The proceedings were held in a closed courtroom after the court had reserved its judgment following the completion of final arguments by both the prosecution and defence.The case arose from allegations made by six women wrestlers, who accused Singh of sexual harassment during his tenure as WFI president.Following the complaints and protests by leading wrestlers at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in 2023, the Delhi Police registered an FIR and later filed a 1,500-page chargesheet against Singh.The chargesheet invoked Sections 354 (assault or criminal force to outrage a woman's modesty), 354A (sexual harassment), 354D (stalking) and 506(1) (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code.Tomar was named as a co-accused and faced allegations of criminal intimidation.The case became one of the biggest controversies in Indian sport, with several prominent wrestlers demanding action against Singh and staging prolonged protests in the national capital.In May 2024, the trial court framed charges against Singh for offences under Sections 354 and 354A of the IPC in connection with allegations made by five women wrestlers. Charges under Section 506(1) relating to criminal intimidation were also framed based on complaints by two wrestlers.Tomar was also charged with criminal intimidation for allegedly threatening one of the complainants.During the trial, the court heard detailed submissions from both sides. The court also examined members of the Special Investigation Team (SIT), including the investigating officer.A separate case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act involving a minor wrestler had earlier been closed after the complainant withdrew her allegations, following which the Delhi Police filed a cancellation report.
Article Summary: Delhi court acquits Brij Bhushan Singh and Vinod Tomar in sexual harassment case. Trial followed nationwide protests by some of the country's top wrestlers. Case arose from allegations made by six women wrestlers, who accused Singh of sexual harassment during his tenure as WFI president.

Article Title: 'Displayed exceptional skill, determination and dedication': PM Modi hails India's Glasgow CWG heroes
Article Text:
PM Narender Modi; and boxer Jaismine Lamboria with India's national flag during the CWG closing ceremony. (PTI Photo)

India signs off with memorable Glasgow campaign



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Focus shifts to Ahmedabad 2030



NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday congratulated the Indian contingent for its impressive campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, praising the athletes for their determination, dedication and skill after the country finished fourth in the medals table with 39 medals.Taking to X after the conclusion of the 11-day sporting extravaganza, the Prime Minister lauded India's medal winners and said their performances would inspire the next generation of athletes."Proud of our contingent's performance at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games. Delighted that India has won 39 medals, including 13 Golds. Congrats to the medal winners," PM Modi posted.He also acknowledged the commitment shown by the athletes throughout the Games."Throughout the Games, our talented athletes have displayed exceptional skill, determination and dedication. Their hard work will keep inspiring our youngsters," he added.The Prime Minister concluded his message by wishing the contingent success in future competitions."My best wishes to the entire Indian contingent for the endeavours ahead. May they continue to give their very best and bring further glory to the nation.#CWG2026."PM Modi's message came a day after India wrapped up another successful Commonwealth Games campaign, securing 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze medals, to finish fourth behind Australia, England and Canada.Although India's tally was lower than the 61 medals won at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games in 2022, the numbers only tell part of the story.The Glasgow programme featured significantly fewer sports, with disciplines such as shooting, wrestling, badminton, hockey and table tennis omitted. In fact, 30 of India's medals in Birmingham had come from sports that were not part of the 2026 Games.Despite travelling with a contingent of just 122 athletes compared to 210 four years ago, India maintained its fourth-place finish while producing an impressive medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with at least one medal.Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh emerged as India's only double medallist, creating history by becoming the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's 5,000m after earlier claiming silver in the 10,000m.India also excelled in boxing, athletics, para sports, judo and weightlifting, underlining the country's growing depth across multiple disciplines.The Glasgow Games concluded with an emotional closing ceremony that officially passed the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India , which will host the landmark centenary edition in Ahmedabad in 2030.Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi received the Commonwealth Games flag on behalf of India during the formal handover ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi in 2010.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi congratulates Indian contingent for its impressive campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. India finished fourth in the medals table with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze medals. India will host the landmark centenary edition in Ahmedabad in 2030.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh acquitted in wrestlers' sexual harassment case; Delhi court clears Vinod Tomar too
Article Text:
File Pic: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh (PTI Photo)

Case followed major wrestlers' protest



Final arguments before verdict



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Delhi court on Monday acquitted former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar in the alleged sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers, bringing an end to a high-profile legal battle that had triggered widespread protests in Indian wrestling.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwani Panwar of the Rouse Avenue Court pronounced the verdict in the case, which stemmed from allegations made by six women wrestlers against Singh during his tenure as the head of the wrestling body.The proceedings were conducted in a closed courtroom, with the court delivering its judgment after hearing arguments from both the prosecution and defence sides.The case dates back to allegations raised by women wrestlers, who accused Singh of sexual harassment during his tenure as WFI president. The allegations led to protests by several top wrestlers at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in 2023, bringing the issue into national focus.Following the complaints, the Delhi Police registered an FIR against Singh and later filed a chargesheet in June 2023 after completing its investigation.The 1,500-page chargesheet invoked provisions under Sections 354 (assault or criminal force against a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment), 354D (stalking) and 506(1) (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code.Singh was accused of offences including sexual harassment, assault or criminal force against women and criminal intimidation, while Tomar was named as a co-accused in connection with allegations of criminal intimidation.In May 2024, the trial court had framed charges against Singh for alleged offences under Sections 354 and 354A of the IPC relating to five women wrestlers. Charges of criminal intimidation under Section 506(1) were also framed against Singh based on allegations made by two wrestlers.Tomar was also charged with criminal intimidation for allegedly threatening one of the complainants.Before the judgment was delivered, the court had heard detailed submissions from both sides.Senior advocate Rebecca John represented the complainants during the final arguments, while the defence team, led by advocate Rajiv Mohan and assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, completed its submissions on June 30.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had reserved the judgment after hearing arguments from the prosecution and defence.The court had also recorded statements of members of the Special Investigation Team (SIT), including an investigating officer, during the trial proceedings.The allegations against Singh had also included a complaint by a minor wrestler under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. However, the complainant later withdrew her statement, following which the Delhi Police filed a cancellation report in the POCSO case and the matter was closed.Singh, a former Bharatiya Janata Party MP, had continued to deny the allegations throughout the proceedings.The acquittal comes after more than two years of legal proceedings that began with protests by some of India's leading wrestlers and became one of the most significant controversies to affect the country's sports administration in recent years.
Article Summary: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Vinod Tomar acquitted in alleged sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers. Case stemmed from allegations made by six women wrestlers against Singh during his tenure as head of the wrestling body. Case dates back to allegations raised by women wrestlers, who accused Singh of sexual harassment. The allegations led to protests by several top wrestlers at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.
Article Summary: India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two- week multinational training camp in Belfast. The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp. Several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.

Article Title: 'Overwhelmed by the love': Ajinkya Rahane thanks fans after retirement announcement
Article Text:
Ajinkya Rahane (ANI Photo)

Cricket fraternity salutes Rahane's remarkable career



A career built on composure and selflessness

NEW DELHI: Days after announcing his retirement from international cricket, former India batter Ajinkya Rahane has broken his silence with an emotional message for fans, admitting he was overwhelmed by the outpouring of love that followed one of the biggest decisions of his career.The 38-year-old, who called time on an international journey spanning more than a decade, thanked supporters from across the cricketing world after receiving countless messages following his retirement announcement."A heartfelt thank you to everyone for your messages, wishes, and support. I'm overwhelmed by the love and will always cherish it," Rahane posted on social media.The message came after tributes poured in from some of the biggest names in world cricket, celebrating a career defined by quiet leadership, resilience and one of India's greatest overseas Test triumphs.Among the many to pay tribute was former India captain Virat Kohli, who described Rahane as his favourite batting partner in Test cricket."Jinks, congratulations on a great career, buddy. You've done wonders for Indian cricket, and you can be very proud of your journey. The safest pair of hands in the slips and my favourite Test batting partner. Wishing you well always. God bless," Kohli wrote.The pair shared one of India's most successful middle-order partnerships, stitching together 10 century stands and 19 fifty-plus partnerships in Tests.Their highest partnership came against New Zealand in Indore, where Kohli scored 211 and Rahane registered a career-best 188 in a mammoth 365-run stand.Batting legend Sachin Tendulkar also reflected on Rahane's career, recalling the first time they batted together for Mumbai in domestic cricket."Congratulations on a remarkable career. The first time we batted together for Mumbai, I saw someone who never chased moments. They came to you because you were willing to do the hard yards for the team. That same quality defined your finest hour in Australia," Tendulkar wrote."You showed that composure isn't the opposite of aggression. It is often what gives a team the confidence to be fearless. Congratulations on a wonderful career! Wishing you and your family all the very best."Rahane announced his retirement from all international formats after representing India in 85 Tests, 90 One-Day Internationals and 20 T20Is between 2011 and 2023.While his numbers — 5,077 Test runs, 2,962 ODI runs and 375 T20I runs — underline his consistency, his greatest contribution came during India's unforgettable 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy triumph in Australia.Stepping in as captain after Virat Kohli returned home following the Adelaide Test, Rahane led an injury-ravaged Indian side to a historic 2-1 series victory. His magnificent century in Melbourne sparked one of the greatest comebacks in Test history before India completed the famous triumph at the Gabba.Former opener Virender Sehwag hailed Rahane as "one of the most underrated cricketers" and praised him for leading India to "its greatest ever overseas Test series win."Cheteshwar Pujara, Shikhar Dhawan, PV Sindhu, Irfan Pathan, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and the Mumbai Cricket Association also paid tribute, highlighting Rahane's humility, calmness and unwavering commitment to the team.
Article Summary: Former India batsman Ajinkya Rahane has announced his retirement from international cricket. The 38-year-old thanked supporters from across the cricketing world after receiving countless messages following his retirement announcement. Former India captain Virat Kohli described Rahane as his favourite batting partner in Test cricket.

Article Title: Judoka Asmita Dey eyes Asian Games, seeks funds for overseas training
Article Text:
Asmita Dey (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

LUCKNOW: Asmita Dey took loans to fund her training in Germany ahead of the Commonwealth Games, which bore rich fruit as she became the first Indian judoka to win a gold medal at the Games in Glasgow. Even as she savours the historic feat, the Uttar Pradesh Police sub-inspector has already set her sights on the Asian Games , scheduled to be held in Japan in Sept.However, a lack of funds for overseas training ahead of the big event is threatening to derail her preparations. Speaking to TOI, Asmita said the Asian Games are her next target, but financial constraints have emerged as a major hurdle.“After winning the gold medal at the Commonwealth Games, my focus is now on the Asian Games. I want to go abroad for special training. I am planning to attend a training programme in Valencia, Spain, from Aug 17 to 22, where many international players and coaches will be present. After that, I want to train in Japan before the Asian Games. But I do not have the funds,” Asmita said.“Before the Commonwealth Games, I took a loan for a special training camp in Germany from May to June. I also take care of all my family's expenses,” she added.Asmita, who hails from Tripura, said her judo journey began at the Tripura Sports School, where she studied from Class 7 to Class 10. In 2019, she joined the Sports Authority of India (SAI) centre in Bhopal for regular training and national camps. In 2025, she obtained a no-objection certificate from Tripura and joined the Uttar Pradesh Judo Association.She said her job in the Uttar Pradesh Police has played a crucial role in supporting her sporting career.“I got a job in UP Police as a constable in 2023. That job played a major role in my life. I manage my expenses from my salary. I am very thankful to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. When I had nothing, the constable job helped me a lot. At the time of joining, the chief minister gave me a welcome letter,” Asmita said.Asmita said the first person she wanted to share her Commonwealth Games gold with was her father, who died seven months ago after suffering a brain stroke. A cycle mechanic, he earned around Rs 300 a day and raised the family in a mud house in a small village in Tripura.Uttar Pradesh Judo Association secretary Munawar Anzar said he would request the state sports department to arrange funds for Asmita's international training.
Article Summary: Asmita Dey became the first Indian judoka to win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games. The Uttar Pradesh Police sub-inspector has already set her sights on the Asian Games. A lack of funds for overseas training ahead of the big event is threatening to derail her preparations.

Article Title: Teen sensation Tanvi Sharma creates history with Taipei Open title
Article Text:
Tanvi Sharma (Image credit: BAI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Seventeen-year-old Tanvi Sharma scripted history on Sunday by capturing her maiden BWF World Tour Super 300 title at the Taipei Open, becoming the youngest champion in the tournament’s history across all categories.The Indian prodigy produced a composed and dominant performance to defeat sixth seed and world No. 21, Nguyen Thuy Linh of Vietnam 21-16, 21-16 in the women’s singles final, capping a dream week in which she dropped just one game.At just 17 years and 222 days, Tanvi surpassed the legendary Tai Tzu Ying’s mark to enter into the tournament’s record books. The triumph also ended India’s 17-year wait for a women’s singles title at the Taipei Open. Tanvi became only the second Indian after Saina Nehwal , who lifted the trophy in 2008, to win the event. Overall, it was India’s third Taipei Open title after Jwala Gutta and V Diju won the mixed doubles crown in 2009.“I didn’t expect to win a title, but I just wanted to give my best. I am really very happy to win this title here,” said Tanvi after her victory.“I took one match at a time, and I’m happy that I played really well throughout the tournament.”Coached by former South Korean international Park Tae-sang, Tanvi showcased exceptional maturity, tactical awareness and deceptive stroke play throughout the tournament.“I was quite nervous, but I just thought I would play my 100 per cent and stick to my game,” she said.“It was hard playing five matches, but I just needed to stay consistent. I have to work harder for the Super 500 and Super 750 tournaments, so I’ll keep working hard,” added Tanvi.Having already beaten Nguyen earlier this season at the US Open, Tanvi entered the final with confidence and immediately seized control. She repeatedly caught the experienced Vietnamese at the net with brilliantly disguised drop shots played with the action of a smash, racing to a 10-2 lead through a combination of cross-court smashes and delicate work at the net.A brief spell of unforced errors allowed Nguyen to reduce the deficit, but Tanvi recovered quickly and surged to 17-9 before clinching the first game at 21-16.Nguyen responded strongly in the second game, opening a 3-0 lead. However, Tanvi steadily wrested back control through patient rallies, precise net play and deceptive drives. She built commanding leads of 15-10 and 18-12 before earning seven championship points.One of the most touching moments came after the match when Tanvi removed her gold medal and placed it around coach Park Taesang’s neck before the pair posed together for photographs.Tanvi’s victory marks another significant milestone in a rapidly blossoming career. Earlier, she became the first Indian to win two medals at a single edition of the BWF World Junior Championships, claiming silver in girls’ singles and bronze in the mixed team event.She was also a member of the Indian squad that won the country’s maiden gold medal at the Asian Team Championships.A former World Junior No. 1, Tanvi reached her first BWF Super 300 final at the 2025 US Open at the age of just 16 and also finished runner-up at both the Odisha Masters Super 100 and Guwahati Masters Super 100.Behind her meteoric rise has been years of relentless hard work and family sacrifice. Her mother, Meena Sharma, a physical education teacher and former national-level volleyball player, learnt badminton herself to coach Tanvi during her early years in Hoshiarpur.The teenager endured gruelling 4 am training sessions before moving to the National Centre of Excellence in Guwahati, where she began training under Park Tae-sang.
Article Summary: Seventeen-year-old Tanvi Sharma scripted history by capturing her maiden BWF World Tour Super 300 title at the Taipei Open. The Indian prodigy produced a composed and dominant performance to defeat sixth seed and world No. 21, Nguyen Thuy Linh of Vietnam. Tanvi became only the second Indian after Saina Nehwal, who lifted the trophy in 2008, to win the event.

Article Title: Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of Sri Lanka series
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah (ICC Photo)

MUMBAI: India have suffered a major setback ahead of the two-Test series against Sri Lanka, with pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah set to miss the tour because of a knee injury.Bumrah, who was picked in the squad subject to fitness, underwent an assessment at the BCCI ’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru on July 30. However, the Board’s medical team has decided against rushing him back into Test cricket before he makes a full recovery.“Bumrah has been ruled out of the Sri Lanka series. His fitness level is currently around 95 per cent, but he is yet to be tested for the demands of the longer format,” a BCCI source told TOI.Bumrah sustained an impact injury to his left knee while fielding during the second ODI against England in Cardiff, forcing him to miss the series finale at Lord’s. The medical staff have advised against risking a premature return.The India squad will assemble in Mumbai on Aug 3 before departing for Sri Lanka the following day. The tour begins with a four-day warm-up match from Aug 7.With the Asian Games in Sept-Oct, a tour of New Zealand later in the year and a five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy at home early next year, the BCCI is keen to manage Bumrah’s workload carefully rather than risk a recurrence.The Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee is expected to announce a replacement shortly. Jammu & Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi is the frontrunner after finishing as the leading wicket-taker in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy with 60 wickets in 10 matches at an average of 12.56.The 29-year-old also trained with the senior squad before the one-off Test against Afghanistan and claimed six wickets in two matches during India A’s recent tour of Sri Lanka.India’s pace attack for the series currently comprises Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and uncapped Gurnoor Brar.
Article Summary: Jasprit Bumrah is ruled out of the two-Test series against Sri Lanka. The 29-year-old sustained an impact injury to his left knee while fielding during the second ODI against England in Cardiff, forcing him to miss the series finale at Lord's. The Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee is expected to announce a replacement shortly.

Article Title: Who is Neel Patel? Indian-origin batting prodigy named in Australia U19 squad for India tour
Article Text:
Neel Patel (Pic credit: Cricket NSW)

Who is Neel Patel?



The habits behind his rapid rise



Australia prepare for challenging India tour

Australia U19 Men’s Squad vs India U19

Kasey Barton (TAS/Mosman CC), Hayden Barbulovic (SA/Tea Tree Gully DCC), Eli Brain (QLD/Northern Suburbs District Cricket Club), Will Byrom (NSW/Northern District CC), Blake Cattle (NSW/Keira CC, Illawarra), Jack Czosnek (VIC/Richmond CC), Spencer Green (QLD/Toombul District Cricket Club), Connor Gregory (SA/Sturt DCC), Charlie Henderson (QLD/University of Queensland Cricket Club), Zed Hollick (WA/Scarborough CC), Matthew Lough (WA/Claremont Nedlands Cricket Club), Neel Patel (NSW/University of NSW Cricket Club), Jacob Pietz (VIC/Camberwell Magpies CC), Patrick Sullivan (VIC/Geelong CC), Theo Tsingos (QLD/Sandgate Redcliffe District Cricket Club), Thomas Vaseo (QLD/Redlands Tigers Cricket Club)

Indian-origin opening batter Neel Patel has earned one of the biggest opportunities of his young career after being named in Australia's Under-19 squad for next month's multi-format tour of India.The New South Wales youngster is among 16 of Australia's brightest emerging cricketers selected for the four-week tour, which will see the visitors play three one-day matches and two four-day games against India U19 across Rajkot and Ahmedabad from September 13 to October 9.For Patel, the selection marks another significant milestone in a rapidly rising career that has already established him as one of Australia's most exciting teenage batting prospects.An elegant opening batter who also bowls handy off-spin, Patel has quickly climbed through Australia's junior cricket pathway thanks to his consistency and maturity at the crease.Representing the University of New South Wales (UNSW) Cricket Club, Patel made headlines at just 16 years of age by becoming one of the youngest players in Sydney Premier Cricket First Grade history after scoring more than 1,000 runs in a single calendar year.He has since added a maiden first-grade century to his growing list of achievements.His performances also earned him selection for Cricket Australia's prestigious Under-19 Men's Talent Camp in Adelaide, where he was identified as one of the country's leading young prospects.Currently opening the batting for New South Wales at junior level, Patel is known for his ability to occupy the crease for long periods while keeping the scoreboard moving. Alongside his batting, he contributes with off-spin, making him a valuable all-round option.Despite his growing reputation, Patel believes there is still plenty of room for improvement.Speaking to Cricket Australia, the teenager revealed he has been working extensively on his back-foot game after receiving advice from his coaches."Batting wise, it's back-foot stuff. I've been given advice from my coaches on how to work on that," Patel said. "Then also fielding, and the strength and fitness side of the game."One of Patel's most unusual habits is maintaining a detailed OneNote journal documenting every innings he plays.After each match, he records what worked well and where improvements are needed, helping him remain accountable for his development."I think it's just to stay on track with what I do and just be accountable," Patel explained. "The OneNote keeps track of my performances; what I did well and what I can improve on for every single game, so I'm always learning."Away from cricket, Patel enjoys cooking, playing chess with his father and building LEGO sets to switch off from the game.Patel's inclusion comes as Cricket Australia announced a 16-player squad featuring some of the nation's most promising youngsters.The team will be coached by experienced mentor Tim Nielsen, while Cricket Australia Head of National Development Sonya Thompson described the tour as an invaluable opportunity for Australia's next generation."Touring India and playing against high-quality opposition in challenging conditions will be a valuable experience and test the players technically and mentally across formats," Thompson said.The month-long series is expected to provide a stern examination for Australia's young cricketers, with Patel set to be one of the players in focus as he returns to his family's country of origin hoping to make a lasting impression against one of world cricket's strongest junior sides.
Article Summary: Neel Patel named in Australia's Under-19 squad for tour of India. The New South Wales youngster is among 16 of Australia's brightest emerging cricketers selected for the four-week tour. The tour will see the visitors play three one- day matches and two four-day games against India.

Article Title: Sri Lanka complete white-ball double with six-wicket win to clinch women's T20I series
Article Text:
Sri Lanka Beat Pakistan

Pakistan's blazing start fails to translate into a match-winning total

Athapaththu sets the tone with explosive counterattack

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Middle order finishes the job in style

Sri Lanka continued their dominance over Pakistan, registering a fourth straight victory in the ongoing white-ball series to clinch the T20I series after already wrapping up the ODI leg. Chasing a challenging target of 176, the hosts cruised to a six-wicket win with 14 balls remaining, extending their impressive run against their Asian rivals.Asked to bat first, Pakistan made a flying start courtesy of their opening pair, who took full advantage of the Powerplay. Shawaal Zulfiqar led the early charge, smashing five boundaries in a single over as the visitors raced to 63 without loss inside the first five overs.However, Sri Lanka gradually wrestled back control after the explosive beginning. The scoring rate dipped through the middle overs before Pakistan lost opener Muneeba Ali at the halfway stage.Chamodi Praboda then struck another crucial blow by dismissing the well-set Shawaal, ensuring Pakistan couldn't fully capitalise on their dominant start. Although Eyman Fatima provided a late boost with an unbeaten 30, the visitors finished on 175, a total that appeared below par considering their explosive opening stand.Pakistan made the ideal start with the ball by removing centurion Imesha Dulani in just the second over. But the breakthrough only brought captain Chamari Athapaththu to the crease, and she immediately shifted the momentum in Sri Lanka's favour.Athapaththu unleashed an attacking display, tearing into the Pakistan bowling attack with a flurry of boundaries. Her rapid 40 off just 14 deliveries ensured Sri Lanka raced to 51 runs inside four overs, erasing any early pressure from the chase.Following Athapaththu's dismissal, Sanjana Kavindi seamlessly carried forward the momentum. She kept the scoreboard ticking with regular boundaries before taking apart spinner Nashra Sandhu with back-to-back sixes around the halfway mark of the innings.Even after Kavindi departed, Sri Lanka never lost control. Harshitha Samarawickrama injected further urgency with a quickfire 24 off 11 balls, while Vishmi Gunaratne also made a useful contribution before being dismissed.With the required rate well under control, Sri Lanka comfortably crossed the finish line in the 18th over, sealing the T20I series in emphatic fashion and completing another commanding performance against Pakistan.
Article Summary: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by six wickets to win the T20I series 2-0. Hosts chased down a target of 176 to win with 14 balls remaining. Chamari Athapaththu and Sanjana Kavindi starred for Sri Lanka.

Article Title: Shashank Singh quits Chhattisgarh, set to join Pondicherry for 2026-27 season
Article Text:

Mumbai: Punjab Kings' vice-captain and prominent IPL batter Shashank Singh has decided to move from Chhattisgarh to Pondicherry for the 2026-27 season. Shashank Singh and Prasad Pawar (Mumbai’s wicketkeeper-batsman) will be Pondicherry’s guest players in the upcoming domestic season. We will finalise a third guest player in a couple of weeks," Cricket Association of Pondicherry's former president P Damodaran told TOI on Sunday.“Yes, I’m quitting Chhattisgarh. I’ve taken the NOC from CSCS and am moving to Pondicherry from the 2026-27 season. I suffered serious shoulder and finger injuries (fracture on the right finger) last season, but the Chhattisgarh State Cricket Sangh didn’t support me at all in this phase. Post the season, they didn’t put my name in the list of players for the Chhattisgarh Cricket Premier League 2026, and my name was also missing in the Chhattisgarh squad which travelled to Bengaluru (Alur) for a pre-season camp. I asked why they didn't put my name. There was no response,” Shashank told TOI on Sunday.“I was told that I only want to play in the IPL, and not for Chhattisgarh in domestic cricket. The reality is that just last year (in Feb 2025), I was adjudged as India's best all-rounder in the white-ball circuit by the BCCI, when I was named as the recipient of the prestigious Lala Amarnath Award for the Best All-Rounder in Domestic Limited Overs Competitions for the 2023-24 season,” Shashank said.The 34-year-old all-rounder had struck 450 runs and taken 11 wickets in seven matches in the Vijay Hazare Trophy, and scored 188 runs in seven games in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy in the 2024-25 season.Shashank is now focusing on becoming a proper white-ball all-rounder this season. “My body is still fresh. This is why I am focusing more on white-ball cricket, and taking a break from red-ball cricket for this season. I am a proper all-rounder. I’m focusing on bowling my full quota of four overs in T20 cricket, for both Pondicherry and for Punjab Kings in the IPL,” Shashank said.The veteran player was in the news for the wrong reasons recently after he and his father, Shailesh Singh, a retired Special Director General of Police, faced an FIR for alleged assault and verbal abuse of their cook named Vipendra Singh. Shashank has, though, denied the allegations. “I’ve been cleared of all the allegations,” he stressed.Shashank had played a key role in Punjab Kings' run to the IPL-2025 final, scoring 350 runs at a strike rate of 153.51, including an unbeaten 61 off just 30 balls in the final against Royal Challengers Bengaluru.Having moved from Bhilai to Mumbai at the age of 16, Shashank played for the DY Patil team in Mumbai's local tournaments. The all-rounder made his Vijay Hazare Trophy and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy debuts for Mumbai in 2015. However, he played just three List A games for Mumbai, whom he represented till 2018. At the age of 27, he switched back to Chhattisgarh.From 2019 onwards, Shashank was a regular in the Chhattisgarh side across formats. In 24 first-class games for the state, he has scored 905 runs at an average of 29.9 and taken 16 wickets at 47.87 with his medium pace. In List A cricket, he has better numbers: 1,054 runs in 35 matches at 40.53 and 37 wickets, while in T20s he averages 25.55 with the bat. In the 2023-24 season, he became the first Indian to score 150-plus runs and take five wickets in the same List A game, a feat he achieved against Manipur.
Article Summary: Punjab Kings' vice-captain Shashank Singh will move to Pondicherry. The 34-year- old will be a guest player for the 2026-27 season. The all-rounder had played a key role in Punjab Kings' run to the IPL-2025 final.

Former India wicketkeeper-batter Deep Dasgupta believes head coach Gautam Gambhir will be under pressure when India begin their two-match Test series against Sri Lanka in Galle on August 15. India have lost Test series against New Zealand, Australia and South Africa under Gambhir, and will now look to bounce back against Sri Lanka.Dasgupta said the pressure will not only be on Gambhir but also on captain Shubman Gill and the rest of the Indian team."As we are saying, two out of three series have been lost. NEW DELHI: A Glasgow-based Indian restaurant deleted its Instagram account after Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain pointed out that its logo and napkins showed an incorrect map of India.The incident happened after the Indian boxing team visited Mister Singh's India - The Home of Curry to celebrate its historic Commonwealth Games 2026 campaign. India finished with a record 10 boxing medals - seven gold and three silver.During the dinner, Lovlina noticed that the map printed on the restaurant's napkins and displayed outside the restaurant did not include India's Northeast.A video of her raising the issue went viral on social media and drew criticism from many users.Lovlina, who is from Assam and won a silver medal in Glasgow, politely raised the issue with the restaurant management."Please don't take this the wrong way. I felt a little hurt by this. In the map of India, our North East is missing. Yes, even outside, the map that's displayed has cut off the North East. Article Title: Nari Shakti drives India's golden charge as women lead Glasgow triumph

8 of India's 13 Commonwealth Games gold medals have been won by women.

Gold medals came in weightlifting, para athletics, judo and boxing.

Five women boxers - Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Priya Ghanghas and Arundhati Choudhary - struck gold.

The performances highlighted the depth of Indian women's sport and inspired a new generation to dream of representing the country on the world stage.

NEW DELHI: India's women emerged as the biggest force behind the country's impressive Commonwealth Games campaign, winning eight of the nation's 13 gold medals and underlining their growing dominance across disciplines. From weightlifting and para athletics to judo and boxing, the women athletes not only contributed significantly to India's medal tally but also defined the country's golden run in Glasgow.The stellar performances reflected the remarkable rise of women's sport in India, with a blend of Olympic champions, established stars and emerging talents delivering on the biggest stage. Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu Saikhom once again showcased her class by adding another CWG title to her illustrious career, while Sharmila Dhankar produced a memorable effort to clinch gold in the women's shot put in para athletics.History was scripted on the judo mat as Asmita Dey became India's first-ever CWG judo gold medallist, adding another milestone to the country's campaign.Indian women's boxing, meanwhile, stamped its authority in spectacular fashion. Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar , Jaismine Lamboria, Priya Ghanghas and Arundhati Choudhary all finished atop the podium, highlighting the remarkable depth India has developed in women's boxing over the past decade.Together, the eight champions have powered India's campaign and reinforced the message that Indian women are no longer merely contenders on the international stage but consistent winners capable of dominating elite competitions.Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president Dr P T Usha, herself a trailblazer for generations of Indian sportswomen, hailed the achievements as a reflection of years of dedication and belief."Seeing India's women win eight of our 13 gold medals fills me with immense pride. These achievements are the result of years of dedication by the athletes, their families, coaches and support teams. Every medal tells the story of perseverance and sacrifice. More importantly, these champions are inspiring countless young girls across India to believe that they too can wear the India jersey and succeed on the world stage. That is the true spirit of Nari Shakti," she said.The performances also mirror a wider transformation taking place across the country, where increasing emphasis on women's empowerment has translated into greater opportunities in sport. Improved access to training facilities, stronger athlete support systems and sustained encouragement for girls to pursue competitive sport have helped create an ecosystem in which talent continues to flourish.Beyond the medals, India's women displayed exceptional team spirit throughout the Games, with senior athletes mentoring younger teammates and celebrating each other's successes. Their performances have inspired millions of young girls across the country, proving that sporting excellence knows no gender.The medals will adorn trophy cabinets, and records may eventually be broken, but the inspiration created by Mirabai Chanu, Sharmila Dhankar, Asmita Dey, Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Priya Ghanghas and Arundhati Choudhary promises to leave a lasting legacy.

Article Title: I've learnt to enjoy every medal win: Lovlina Borgohain
Article Text:
Lovlina Borgohain (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It isn’t easy being an athlete. The constant pressure of perfor mance, making sacrifices at various stages of their career and rarely finding moments to appreciate the victories, gets too much to handle at times.Thirteen years after living an athlete’s life, Tokyo Games bronze medallist boxer Lovlina Borgohain has realised that a lot of her time has gone more in overthinking and less in celebrating. So, when she had to settle for silver at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Saturday, she said she needed to work harder, but she also cel-ebrated the silver rather than ruing over the missed gold.“I feel I need to work even harder, though my prepara-tion this time was solid and I had put in good effort. I missed out by a small margin, but I am happy. Given my long journey with many ups and downs, I am making a comeback, which is extremely important to me, and maintaining that momentum is key,” Lovlina told TOI from Glasgow.“Now, I enjoy every medal I win. Earlier, if I didn’t reach my expected outcome, I used to get very sad. Then I would immediately fixate on needing to perform in the next match. But I realized that because of that mindset, I couldn’t even enjoy my medals for a long time, and I missed out on many moments I could have celebrated,” said Lovlina, who won her first CWG medal in her third participation.The Assam athlete, who started boxing in 2013, said athletes have to make many sacrifices in their respective journeys, and she was no dif-ferent.“Staying away from family was the hardest part for me. Beyond that, there are frequent injuries, and you must isolate yourself from many normal things. We constantly feel that even a minor distraction — like going out some-where or eating something outside — might negatively impact our performance. A huge chunk of time goes into overthinking whether an action will cause a problem. In a way, having to carefully evaluate every single decision is a sacrifice in itself,” the Khel Ratna awardee said.Quitting things that she loved for the sake of her game has made her a completely different person.“I used to love sweets a lot. But I told myself I shouldn’t eat them, so I completely stopped. Now, I don’t even crave them anymore. I don’t miss not having sweets or ice cream,” she said.After following a routine for so many years, Lovlina said it will be difficult to go back to the old life again.“But we still enjoy it, because if we weren’t boxing and lived a nor mal life, we probably wouldn’t fit into that either. This has become our life, and we love living it this way.”After reeling under constant pressure of winning a medal and doing well, Lovlina said that she has made peace with not winning a medal too.“There were many moments I missed out on that I could have enjoyed more. Sometimes I do feel a bit of regret about those things, but once you realize it, everything changes from that moment on. The whole perspective shifts. Right now, losing doesn’t sadden me as much as winning a medal makes me happy — and seeing my team-mates perform so well makes me even happier,” she said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Saturday. The Assam athlete said athletes have to make many sacrifices in their respective journeys, and she was no dif-ferent. The Khel Ratna awardee said staying away from family was the hardest part for her.

Article Title: She lost her gold — then won it again: Why Melanie Woods claimed the David Dixon Award
Article Text:
Commonwealth Sport president Donald Rukare, centre, presents the David Dixon Award to Melanie Woods. (PTI/AP Photo)

ALSO READ:

A champion tested like never before



Winning twice to remove all doubt



Why Melanie Woods received the David Dixon Award

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Scottish wheelchair racer Melanie Woods capped an unforgettable home Commonwealth Games by winning the prestigious David Dixon Award, recognising her as the outstanding athlete of Glasgow 2026 after a campaign defined not only by two gold medals but also by extraordinary resilience, sportsmanship and composure under unprecedented circumstances.The David Dixon Award, voted for by fellow athletes, honours the competitor who best combines sporting excellence, fair play and contribution to their team. Woods embodied all three qualities during one of the most dramatic stories of the Glasgow Games.Her remarkable journey saw her win the women's T54 1500m title twice in less than 40 hours before adding a second gold in the T54 400m, making her one of the defining faces of the Games.The defining moment of Woods' Games came in the women's T54 1500m final, where she initially stormed to victory in a Commonwealth Games record time of 3:33.39.However, celebrations were short-lived.A chaotic first-lap crash involving several athletes prompted a series of protests and appeals. Canada's Nandini Sharma collided with Mauritius' Noemi Alphonse, triggering a chain reaction that also brought down Australia's Eliza Ault-Connell, Scotland's Joanna Robertson and England's Ellis Kottas.Although Woods had avoided the incident and crossed the finish line well clear of the field, officials later upheld appeals from Australia and Mauritius, voiding the result and ordering a complete rerun of the final — one of the most extraordinary decisions in Commonwealth Games history.Instead of expressing frustration after losing a gold medal she believed she had rightfully earned, Woods accepted the ruling with grace, respecting both the appeals process and her fellow competitors.Her calm response quickly became as admired as her racing ability.Less than 40 hours later, Woods returned to Scotstoun Stadium with the pressure of having to prove herself all over again.She responded in the best possible fashion.Taking the lead within the opening 100 metres, the Scot controlled the race from start to finish and crossed the line in a new Commonwealth Games record of 3:32.20, improving upon the mark she had already set in the original final."I'm happy, I'm excited, but it feels like relief, to be honest," Woods said after reclaiming the title. "It's created a bit of a storyline and I feel like people have been following for the plot, so I'm just happy to be able to do it again."Remarkably, Woods had barely any time to celebrate.Just 90 minutes after reclaiming her 1500m crown, she returned to the track for the heats of the women's T54 400m, where she qualified fastest for the final.The following evening, she completed a memorable double by winning the 400m title to secure her second gold medal of Glasgow 2026.The performances cemented her place as Scotland's standout athlete at the home Games.While medal winners often dominate headlines, the David Dixon Award has never been based solely on podium finishes.It recognises athletes who combine exceptional performances with integrity, respect and leadership.Woods' response to the controversial rerun perfectly captured those values.Rather than allowing disappointment to overshadow the event, she accepted the unprecedented decision with dignity, returned to the start line and produced an even faster, more convincing victory.Her resilience, sportsmanship and outstanding performances earned widespread admiration from fellow competitors, who voted her the recipient of the David Dixon Award.By the end of Glasgow 2026, Melanie Woods had achieved something few athletes ever experience — winning the same Commonwealth Games title twice, setting two Games records and leaving as the athlete who best represented the spirit of the Games.
Article Summary: Woods won the David Dixon Award for the outstanding athlete of Glasgow 2026. The award honours the competitor who best combines sporting excellence, fair play and contribution to their team. Woods embodied all three qualities during one of the most dramatic stories of the Glasgow Games.

Article Title: Over to Ahmedabad! Neeraj Chopra, PT Usha receive CWG flag as India's 2030 countdown begins
Article Text:
CWG 2026 closing ceremony

Glasgow hands over the baton to Ahmedabad



India showcases culture, unity and ambition



India signs off with a memorable campaign

NEW DELHI: The 2026 Commonwealth Games came to a spectacular close in Glasgow on Sunday, bringing the curtain down on 11 days of sporting excellence and signalling the beginning of a new chapter for India. In a symbolic and emotional handover ceremony, Scotland formally passed the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India, with Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha receiving them on behalf of the nation as the countdown to the centenary 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad officially began.The glittering closing ceremony at the OVO Hydro celebrated Scotland's rich cultural heritage before seamlessly transitioning into a vibrant showcase of India's traditions, music and modern aspirations, underscoring Ahmedabad's readiness to welcome the Commonwealth in four years' time.India also departed Glasgow with plenty to celebrate on the sporting front, finishing fourth in the medal standings with an impressive haul of 39 medals — 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze — despite competing with a much smaller contingent and in a significantly reduced sporting programme.The emotional centrepiece of the evening came during the official handover ceremony, where Glasgow formally transferred hosting responsibilities to India.The Commonwealth Games flag made its symbolic journey across the arena before being presented through a distinguished line of dignitaries. Glasgow's Lord Provost Jacqueline McLaren handed it to Commonwealth Games Scotland vice-chair Susan Jackson, Scottish netball player Emily Nicholl, Commonwealth Sport president Dr Donald Rukare, Olympic gold medallist Neeraj Chopra, IOA president PT Usha and finally Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, completing the ceremonial transfer.The occasion marked the official start of the road to Ahmedabad 2030, when India will host the Commonwealth Games for only the second time after New Delhi in 2010. The 2030 edition carried added significance as the centenary Commonwealth Games.Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh, representing King Charles III, formally declared the Games closed while inviting athletes from across the Commonwealth to reunite in India."Thanks for the manner in which you have competed, officiated, supported and organised the Games. You have once again brought the spirit and value of the Commonwealth tonight. Thank you, Glasgow," he said."I call upon athletes of all countries and territories to come to Ahmedabad, India in four years' time to celebrate the 24th Commonwealth Games in what will be the centenary of the Games."Following the formal handover, India delivered a breathtaking cultural presentation built around the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — "The World is One Family."The showcase unfolded in three acts celebrating India's diversity, artistic traditions and sporting legacy while inviting the Commonwealth to Ahmedabad.Actor Manushi Chhillar led a visually stunning opening performance commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram, accompanied by hundreds of dancers performing against immersive digital backdrops. Acclaimed composer Shankar Mahadevan's orchestral score blended Indian classical traditions with contemporary arrangements.A specially curated film then introduced Ahmedabad to the world, portraying Gujarat as a land where centuries-old heritage coexists with modern infrastructure and innovation. The presentation highlighted sport as an integral part of Indian civilisation while positioning Ahmedabad as an ideal host for the landmark centenary Games.One of the ceremony's defining moments came through an Indo-Scottish musical collaboration titled The Cultural Jugalbandi, where sitar maestro Rishab Sharma performed alongside celebrated Scottish musician Ross Ainslie. Their fusion of Indian classical music with Scottish pipes symbolised the seamless passing of the baton between the outgoing and incoming hosts.The Indian segment concluded with Shankar Mahadevan performing alongside his sons Siddharth and Shivam Mahadevan, delivering stirring renditions of iconic songs including Suno Gaur Se Duniya Walon, Bhaag Milkha Bhaag, Ae Watan and Lehara Do. Gujarati singer Bhoomi Trivedi added a special tribute to the host state, ensuring Ahmedabad remained firmly at the heart of India's invitation to the Commonwealth.Meanwhile, women's 57kg boxing gold medallist Jaismine Lamboria proudly carried the Indian flag during the closing ceremony.Beyond the celebrations, Glasgow proved to be another successful Commonwealth Games for India.The Indian contingent finished fourth with 39 medals — 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze — behind Australia, England and Canada. Hosts Scotland also won 39 medals but finished below India due to a lower silver-medal count.Although India's total fell short of the 61 medals won in Birmingham four years ago, the comparison hardly reflects the reality of Glasgow. The 2026 programme excluded several sports where India has traditionally excelled, including shooting, wrestling, badminton, hockey and table tennis. In fact, 30 of India's medals in Birmingham had come from disciplines omitted this time.Despite travelling with just 122 athletes compared to 210 in Birmingham, India maintained its fourth-place finish while recording an outstanding medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals.Boxing spearheaded India's charge with an exceptional 10-medal haul, including seven gold medals, reaffirming the country's growing dominance in the sport. Athletics also scripted history, highlighted by Gulveer Singh becoming the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's 5,000m after earlier claiming silver in the 10,000m, making him India's only double medallist in Glasgow.India's para athletes enjoyed their most successful Commonwealth Games campaign ever, while judoka, weightlifters and track and field stars consistently added to the medal tally across the 11-day competition.
Article Summary: The 2026 Commonwealth Games came to a spectacular close in Glasgow on Sunday, bringing the curtain down on 11 days of sporting excellence. In a symbolic and emotional handover ceremony, Scotland formally passed the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India. India also departed Glasgow with plenty to celebrate on the sporting front, finishing fourth in the medal standings with an impressive haul of 39 medals.

Article Title: Gulveer Singh’s 'double' speaks of patience and precision
Article Text:
Gulveer Singh after winning silver in 10,000m and (pic right) with coach Scott Simmons (left) after winning bronze in 5,000m

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Few combinations in athletics are as revered — or as punishing — as the 5000m and 10,000m. Yet India’s Gulveer Singh rode both challenges in Glasgow, adding a bronze in the 5000m to the silver he had claimed in the 10,000m days earlier to script one of Indian athletics’ finest Commonwealth Games campaigns.In doing so, Gulveer became the first Indian to win two athletics medals at a single Commonwealth Games, leaving long-time coach Scott Simmons beaming with pride.“Honestly, all I knew after meeting the Indian distance runners at SAI Bengaluru was that they had a lot of untapped potential,” Simmons told TOI from Glasgow on Sunday.That potential was on full display in Glasgow. If the 10,000m tested Gulveer’s endurance, the 5000m demanded patience and precision — qualities he displayed throughout the race.Staying on the inside rail to cover the shortest possible distance, Gulveer remained between third and eighth spots for much of the race, resisting the temptation to make unnecessary moves.It was all part of the plan.“It was important not to get boxed in or behind with so many runners, and so many very good runners, in one heat,” Simmons explained.Then when eventual winner Mathew Kipchumba Kipsang of Kenya surged into the lead at the start of the final lap, Gulveer bided his time, waiting for the right moment to launch his challenge.Simmons knew his ward possessed the finishing speed to make patience pay.“What has impressed me the most is his last 400m, 200m and 100m finishing speed. I didn’t see that coming until his 5K at LA Track Fest this spring, where he ran 13:03.93. He was able to outkick true 1500m/5000m runners off a relatively fast pace,” Simmons said.With about 200 metres remaining, the battle for the remaining two podium places came down to Gulveer, Australia’s Ky Robinson and Kenya’s Cornelius Kemboi. For a brief moment, it appeared Gulveer would claim silver, with Kemboi settling for bronze.However, Robinson, the 10,000m champion, produced a brilliant late kick to snatch silver, while Gulveer did just enough to hold off Kemboi and secure bronze in 13:24.95, completing a historic Commonwealth Games campaign.Despite the short turnaround between the two races, Simmons revealed there was little deviation from the routine that had helped Gulveer arrive in Glasgow in peak condition. “After the 10,000m silver, we approached recovery like we always do with a focus on sleep, massage, diet and, very importantly, easy aerobic running,” he said.Simmons, however, believes there is still plenty of room for the 28-year-old Indian to improve.“While Commonwealth Games is one of the competitive arenas for long-distance running, the World Championships and Olympic Games are even tougher. Gulveer needs to continue to improve, especially his finishing kick,” he added.At the same time, the American coach believes his success can inspire a new generation of Indian distance runners, provided they receive the right support.“I think Gulveer’s success will change the belief system of Indian distance runners,” said Simmons, who also coached Avinash Sable to the men’s 3000m steeplechase silver at Birmingham Commonwealth Games.“Do I think other Indians can get to this level? Of course, as long as they have the support for training and competitions abroad and are willing to commit and sacrifice and not look for shortcuts.”
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh is the first Indian to win two athletics medals at a single Commonwealth Games. The 28-year-old won silver in the 10,000m and a bronze in the 5000m. His coach Scott Simmons believes his success can inspire a new generation of Indian distance runners, provided they receive the right support.

India signed off from the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with 39 medals — 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze. The contingent fell short of the 50-medal mark that India had reached at every Commonwealth Games since 2002.With several medal-rich sports missing from the programme because of financial constraints in hosting the Games — after the event was moved from Victoria in Australia to Glasgow — expectations were lower than in previous editions. Even so, India found success in new events, celebrated new athletes and produced several landmark performances.The contingent did not add to its medal tally on the final day, but the campaign ended with highlights that included a record boxing performance, India's best-ever showing in para sports at the Commonwealth Games, and the country's strongest judo campaign in the history of the event.Weightlifting gave India its first medals of the Games, returning with eight medals — one gold, six silver and one bronze. Mirabai Chanu once again led the way by becoming the first Indian weightlifter to win three successive Commonwealth Games gold medals.India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, and 38 of them returned with medals, with Gulveer Singh winning two medals. The country finished in the top five of the overall medal table.Although the tally was lower than the 61 medals won at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, India had sent a much larger contingent of 210 athletes then. In Glasgow, around 31% of the contingent won medals, compared to 29% in Birmingham.India's four-member women's wheelchair basketball team created history by becoming the country's first para team in the sport to qualify for the Commonwealth Games. They finished at the bottom of their group.Among the eight Indian gymnasts, only Tapan Mohanty and Protistha Samanta reached event finals. India has now gone three Commonwealth Games without a gymnastics medal since its last one in 2014.India's 32-member athletics squad returned with 10 medals — five silver and five bronze.Neeraj Chopra settled for silver in the javelin throw, while debutant Yash Vir Singh joined him on the podium with bronze. Tejaswin Shankar became the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games decathlon medal despite competing with an injury. Gulveer Singh completed a historic distance-running campaign by winning silver in the 10,000m and bronze in the 5000m.India's 11 para athletes won six medals, making it one of the country's strongest-performing contingents. The medals came from three events, with India recording three double podium finishes, including two one-two finishes.After winning gold and silver in Birmingham four years ago, India's six-member bowls team returned without a medal.India's boxers delivered the country's biggest success of the Games, winning 10 medals — seven gold and three silver. Ten of the 14 boxers in the squad reached the podium, improving the medal conversion rate from 58% in Birmingham to 71% in Glasgow.World champion Jaismine Lamboria won gold, while Sakshi Chaudhary continued her rise after earlier defeating two world champions in domestic competition. Preeti Pawar, Ankush Panghal, Sachin Siwach, Arundhati Choudhary and Priya Ghanghas also won gold medals. Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal finished with silver medals.India's judokas enjoyed their best Commonwealth Games campaign, returning with four medals, including two gold medals.India's seven-member para powerlifting team arrived with high expectations, but many athletes lifted below their personal bests. Jhandu Kumar was the only Indian to win a medal.Competing against strong teams such as Australia, India's swimmers did not win a medal and most finished below their best timings.India did not win a medal in para swimming.India's track cyclists, including Ronaldo Singh Laitonjam and David Beckham Elkatohchoongo, again finished without a medal.Sixteen-year-old Lisha Das competed without the support she needed after administrative delays left her without a female chaperone and without her aerodynamic suit. She was the youngest athlete at the Games and received strong support from the Glasgow crowd.India won eight medals in weightlifting. Only three of the 10 medal-winning lifters from Birmingham returned to compete in Glasgow.India's weightlifting programme continues to face challenges because of doping cases, which led to the country's quota being reduced from 16 athletes to 11.Mirabai Chanu won gold once again, while Rishikanta Singh, Ajaya Babu and Lovepreet Singh set Commonwealth Games records in the snatch event. Gyaneshwari Yadav set a new national record on her way to winning a silver medal.
Article Summary: India signed off from the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with 39 medals — 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze. The contingent fell short of the 50-medal mark that India had reached at every Commonwealth Games since 2002. India's 32-member athletics squad returned with 10 medals — five silver and five bronze.
