Article Title: Raengdai FC: A football fairytale from conflict-hit Manipur
Article Text:
Image credit: TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Eduardo Galeano, in his sports writing masterpiece, “Football in Sun and Shadow”, writes that “a reporter once asked German theologian Dorothee Sölle, ‘How would you explain happiness to a child?’ ‘I wouldn’t explain it,’ she answered. ‘I’d toss him a ball and let him play.”The game of football holds the power to elicit joy not just in the one with the ball at his feet but also in the others cherishing its magic from off the field, sometimes even when the lives on both ends of the field are caught in an unfortunate strife.That’s the reality of the people of Noney in Manipur — around 63 km west of capital Imphal — and home to Zeliangrong community, comprising Zeme, Liangmai, Rongmei, and Inpui tribes.After “insurgency”, “militant attacks”, “killings” and “curfews” dominated most headlines from the region in the last couple of years, football has brought them in the limelight in the form of Raengdai FC – the club from the region that has been ascending the Indian football ladder with consistency and swiftness.The latest achievement for the four-year-old club was their historic debut in Durand Cup with a 1-0 victory over last season’s quarterfinalists, Indian Navy.“There was naturally a bit of nervousness because of their quality and experience, but that never stopped us from believing in ourselves,” said Raengdai head coach Birbal Singh Kshetrimayum.Raengdai won the Manipur Premier League in 2024 and got the chance to play in I-League 3 during 2024-25 — a chance that they grabbed with both hands. They then won the AIFF competition upon debut to earn promotion into I-League 2 for the upcoming season.It’s the story of a journey that began on Nov 6, 2022, at Centre Point Food Plaza in Imphal when football enthusiasts in the community got together to find a pathway for the youngsters, who they believed had talent aplenty, to make a career in football.“When we founded FC Raengdai, our vision was simple — to create a proper grassroots football pathway for Zeliangrong community. We knew there was plenty of talent in our villages and towns, but many young players lacked the opportunity and platform to showcase their abilities,” says club general secretary Napoleon Rongmei. “FC Raengdai was created to change that.”And it did change the football landscape in the area. It showed the footballing talents the path towards “building a brighter future for the next generation of footballers”.It was at this juncture, on May 3, 2023, that the conflict began in Manipur. With sports across the region coming to a halt, it had its impact even on the newly formed club, too. There was no football activity for two years and it eventually resumed in 2024.But having their training facilities in Imphal helped, as the players could be away from the friction of the conflict and focus on their game.With players not just from Zeliangrong community but from all over the state, Raengdai built a squad, competed and won the 33rd NM Gupta Football Tournament 2024 in Silchar.And when the call came from MPL — the premier club competition in the state — to participate, Raengdai etched their name in Manipur football by emerging champions of the 2nd edition in 2025.Striker Tingkaochun Gangmei, who began playing football in the local grounds, asserts: “Joining FC Raengdai in 2023 was a turning point in my career. It is my first senior club, and together we competed in the Manipur Premier League before earning promotion through I-League 3. Now, to represent FC Raengdai in our first-ever Durand Cup is something I never imagined as a child playing in Khoupum Valley. It makes me proud not only for myself but also for my family and everyone back home. ”Noney also shares Manipur’s higher literacy rate, ranking 10th nationally, and parents in the area didn’t think of football as a better option compared to studies, for their children.“In a typical Rongmei Naga family, football is rarely considered a viable career option. Thinking outside the box and letting my son become a footballer was one of the hardest decisions my family ever made,” said midfielder Gaisuangmei Kamei’s father.“Initially, as parents, we wanted him to pursue formal education at school. However, we ultimately chose to respect his choice. Looking back now, I realize that it was not a bad decision at all.”It was those collective decisions that aided the rise of the community-funded club that, despite financial struggles, is becoming a growing name in Indian football scene.On Monday, they will be at Khuman Lampak Stadium — expected to be packed with fans — for their second match of Durand Cup, incidentally a Manipur derby against TRAU FC.“In a match like this, the crowd can create extra pressure, but that’s part of football. I have told the players that they must be mentally strong, physically ready and enjoy the occasion rather than be overwhelmed by it,” said Kshetrimayum.As for the community back home and in the stands, they will look to Raengdai to once again make the headlines for its footballing merit.
Article Summary: FC Raengdai is a Manipur-based football club. The club was formed in 2022 to help local players make a career in the game. They won the Manipur Premier League in 2024 and got the chance to play in I-League 3 during 2024-25.

Article Title: Gianni Infantino was to earn $30m base salary if FIFA's plan to sell World Cup stakes went through: reports
Article Text:
FILE - FIFA President Gianni Infantino follows an international friendly soccer match between Iran and Costa Rica, in Antalya, southern Turkey, Tuesday, March 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Riza Ozel, File)

Reports claim Infantino was set for $30 million salary



FFE proposal sparked unprecedented backlash



UEFA says confidence in FIFA leadership has been lost



FIFA disputes reports and explains withdrawal



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fallout continues despite proposal being shelved



Gianni Infantino was reportedly in line to receive a $30 million annual base salary under FIFA's now-abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project, according to reports, adding another controversial dimension to a proposal that ultimately collapsed following widespread opposition from football's governing bodies and member associations.The reported remuneration plan surfaced just days after FIFA officially withdrew the proposal to create FFE, a new commercial entity that would have overseen FIFA's competitions while allowing private investors to acquire a minority stake in its commercial rights. The project was abandoned after strong resistance from UEFA, Concacaf, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), national football associations and senior figures within FIFA itself.According to The Times, cited by multiple British publications, the long-term vision for the FFE project would have seen Infantino assume the role of chief executive or commissioner of the new commercial entity.In that position, the FIFA president was reportedly set to receive an annual base salary of approximately $30 million, excluding any additional performance-related bonuses or incentives.The reports suggested the proposal extended beyond attracting private investment into FIFA competitions and envisaged a new executive structure under the commercial arm.FIFA, however, has rejected suggestions that such a remuneration package or executive arrangement was ever formally proposed.The controversy centred on FIFA's proposal to establish FIFA Forward Enterprise, which would have allowed outside investors to purchase a minority stake in the commercial rights of competitions including the FIFA World Cup.As previously reported, the proposal triggered fierce opposition across world football.UEFA's 55 member associations unanimously rejected the plan and warned they would boycott FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, if the proposal proceeded. Concacaf and the AFC subsequently joined UEFA in publicly opposing the project, while FIFA President Gianni Infantino's senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned in protest, describing the proposal as "a bad deal for football."Faced with mounting resistance, FIFA eventually withdrew the proposal before any vote took place.Although FIFA abandoned the project, UEFA insisted the decision alone was not enough to restore confidence.In a strongly worded statement, the European governing body said:"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account."UEFA added:"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental."The statement concluded with perhaps its strongest criticism:"No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family."The English Football Association also backed UEFA's position, saying:"We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."Concacaf likewise called for "a comprehensive reckoning" of Infantino's presidency, describing the controversy as "a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first."Throughout the controversy, FIFA maintained that FFE remained only a consultation proposal rather than a finalised commercial structure.After confirming the project would no longer proceed, Infantino said:"The FFE project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed."He added:"And, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders."Explaining the decision to abandon the proposal, Infantino continued:"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place."He concluded:"Our purpose has always been, and will always be, to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that most need our support."While FIFA's decision brought an end to the FFE project, questions surrounding its origins and governance continue to reverberate across world football.The reported $30 million salary plan, although disputed by FIFA, has added fresh scrutiny to a proposal that had already prompted boycott threats, public resignations and widespread criticism from confederations representing more than half of FIFA's 211 member associations.Even with the proposal now withdrawn, the debate over FIFA's governance and leadership shows little sign of ending as stakeholders continue to examine how the controversial project advanced as far as it did before ultimately being abandoned.
Article Summary: Reports claim Infantino was set for $30 million salary. FIFA disputes reports and explains withdrawal of proposal. UEFA says confidence in FIFA leadership has been lost. Concacaf calls for a "comprehensive reckoning" of the FIFA president.

Vinicius remains focused on Real Madrid



Fresh speculation surrounding Vinicius Jr's future at Real Madrid has prompted a strong response from his representatives, with Roc Nation Sports publicly condemning what it described as "fake" and "damaging" reports targeting its clients.The statement comes after days of renewed reports linking the Brazil international with Arsenal, while uncertainty continues over his contract situation at Real Madrid. Although the agency did not mention Vinicius by name, the timing of the statement has drawn attention given the growing transfer speculation surrounding several of its football clients.On Sunday, Michael Yormark, President of Roc Nation Sports International, shared a statement on Instagram criticising sections of the media for publishing what the agency described as inaccurate stories.The statement read: "Roc Nation Sports International and our entire team cannot stand idle when unprofessional and uninformed media publish fake and damaging information for attention-seeking purposes."It continued: "This is especially unacceptable when it personally targets our clients without any foundation."The agency concluded with another pointed message, adding: "It is disruptive, harmful and libellous.Media outlets and journalists need to hold themselves more accountable."While no individual player was identified, Roc Nation represents several high-profile footballers, including Vinicius Jr, Endrick and Yan Diomande, all of whom have featured prominently in recent transfer reports.The agency's intervention follows another week of speculation over Vinicius' future, with multiple reports suggesting Arsenal are monitoring the Brazilian's contract situation at Real Madrid.The winger is entering the final year of his current contract, fuelling suggestions that several clubs are keeping a close eye on developments.Ahead of Arsenal's pre-season friendly victory over Girona, manager Mikel Arteta was asked directly about reports linking the Gunners with Vinicius.When the Brazilian's name was first mentioned, Arteta smiled before later responding more broadly to Arsenal's transfer plans."We are very active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear," Arteta said."We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else."Arteta neither confirmed nor denied any interest in Vinicius, instead reiterating that Arsenal remain active in the transfer market as they continue strengthening the squad ahead of the new season.The agency's statement also arrives amid reports involving another of its clients, teenage winger Yan Diomande.According to Spanish newspaper , Diomande's proposed move to Real Madrid has been delayed by an alleged dispute between Roc Nation and Maxidel Management, the agency owned by former Ivory Coast international Max Gradel.The report claimed Maxidel has filed a complaint with FIFA alleging a breach of contract after Real Madrid negotiated with Roc Nation during discussions over the player's transfer.Neither Roc Nation nor Real Madrid has publicly commented on those claims.Despite persistent transfer speculation, Vinicius remains a Real Madrid player and continues preparing for the new season.The Brazilian has established himself as one of the club's most influential attackers in recent years, while Real Madrid are continuing preparations under José Mourinho, who returned as head coach ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.With Vinicius' contract entering its final year and transfer rumours continuing to circulate, the latest statement from Roc Nation makes clear that the agency intends to challenge reporting it believes is inaccurate, even as speculation over the winger's future continues.
Article Summary: Roc Nation Sports issues strongly worded statement condemning what it describes as "fake" and "damaging" reports targeting its clients. Statement comes after days of renewed reports linking the Brazil international with Arsenal. Agency's statement also arrives amid reports involving another of its clients, teenage winger Yan Diomande.

Article Title: Leandro Paredes faces three assault charges but little-known FIFA loophole could spare Argentina star
Article Text:
Argentina's Leandro Paredes trains for the World Cup soccer tournament Friday, July 10, 2026, in Kansas City, Kan. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

Paredes facing the most serious charges after final altercation

Spain's Gavi, left, falls as he scuffles with Argentina's Leandro Paredes (5) and Thiago Almada during the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)

Why Paredes could escape serving any suspension

Argentina's Lionel Messi (10) and Leandro Paredes (5) stand on the pitch after the team's loss in the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Abbie Parr)

FIFA has the power to extend bans worldwide

"If the infringement is serious, in particular but not limited to discrimination, manipulation of football matches and competitions, misconduct against match officials, or forgery and falsification, as well as sexual abuse or harassment, the member associations, confederations, and other organising sports bodies shall request that the Disciplinary Committee extend the sanctions they have imposed so as to have worldwide effect (worldwide extension)."

Referee Joao Pinheiro, of Portugal, gives a yellow card to Argentina's Leandro Paredes (5) during the World Cup quarterfinal soccer match in Kansas City, Mo., Saturday, July 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Reed Hoffmann)

What Paredes has said about his Argentina future

Wider disciplinary investigation continues

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Argentina players hold a banner with the words "The Malvinas are Argentine", referring to the Falkland Islands, at the end of the World Cup semifinal soccer match between England and Argentina in Atlanta, Wednesday, July 15, 2026.(AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

Argentina midfielder faces multiple assault charges following final defeat to Spain, but comments on his international future may prove significantThe 32-year-old has been charged with three counts of assault after Argentina's 1-0 extra-time defeat to Spain at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. While FIFA's disciplinary regulations leave him facing a potentially lengthy international ban if found guilty, an unusual loophole in the governing body's rules means the punishment may never ultimately take effect.FIFA has opened disciplinary proceedings against several players and officials from both teams following a series of confrontations after the final whistle.Paredes is facing the most serious allegations, with three separate assault charges brought against the Boca Juniors midfielder.Television footage appeared to show him first kicking and shoving Spain defender Eric García before grabbing him by the throat during a confrontation. Moments later, he was involved in another incident with midfielder Gavi, where he allegedly grabbed the Spaniard before wrestling him to the ground as tempers continued to flare.Argentina teammate Thiago Almada was also involved in the altercation with Gavi and has subsequently been charged with unsporting behaviour.Nahuel Molina has been charged with two assault offences—one completed and one attempted—as well as unsporting behaviour, while Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala faces one assault charge. Spain midfielder Gavi has also been cited for unsporting behaviour.FIFA is currently reviewing the available evidence before allowing all respondents the opportunity to present their positions before any sanctions are imposed.Under Article 14 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code, violent conduct and assault offences carry a minimum suspension of three matches.If FIFA finds Paredes guilty on all three assault charges, he could theoretically receive a suspension totalling nine international matches, although reports have suggested a five or six-match ban is viewed as the more likely outcome.However, comments made by Paredes after the World Cup have created a potential avenue through which he may never actually serve the punishment.The midfielder has openly admitted he is considering retiring from international football following Argentina's defeat in the final.Should he decide to end his Argentina career before any suspension is served, an international ban would effectively become irrelevant unless FIFA chooses to extend the sanction beyond national team competitions.That possibility is governed by Article 70 of FIFA's Disciplinary Code.The regulation allows FIFA to extend sanctions beyond international football and apply them across all domestic and international competitions worldwide in particularly serious cases.The disciplinary code states:Although the listed offences do not specifically include violent conduct between players, the regulation makes clear the examples are "in particular but not limited to" those categories.FIFA has previously exercised that authority in exceptional circumstances, most notably in 2014 when Luis Suárez's suspension for biting Italy defender Giorgio Chiellini during the World Cup was extended worldwide, preventing him from participating in any football-related activity for four months.Such interventions remain relatively rare, however, meaning any decision to impose a worldwide suspension on Paredes would ultimately rest with FIFA's Disciplinary Committee.Shortly after Argentina's defeat, Paredes posted a message on Instagram thanking his teammates and supporters without addressing the post-match incidents."It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history!!" he wrote.Upon returning to Boca Juniors, however, the experienced midfielder acknowledged that his international future remains uncertain."It's been a magnificent journey," Paredes said. "It will be very difficult to maintain this level and ensure that the group continues to function in this way. Decisions must be made calmly. I don't yet know if I'm fit enough to continue. It's a process that needs to be digested and carefully considered."The comments have become increasingly significant as FIFA's disciplinary investigation progresses, with any eventual retirement potentially altering how a suspension would be enforced.Paredes is one of several individuals under investigation following the chaotic scenes after the World Cup final.Alongside the charges against Molina, Almada, Ayala and Gavi, FIFA has also opened proceedings against the Argentine Football Association (AFA).The federation is facing allegations relating to discriminatory chants and gestures, breaches of match and security regulations, delays to kick-off, inappropriate messages displayed by players and supporters, and the throwing of objects.If those charges are upheld, the AFA could face substantial financial penalties and, in more serious circumstances, partial or complete stadium closures for future international fixtures.With FIFA's disciplinary process still ongoing, Paredes' sporting future now hinges on two separate decisions: the sanction imposed by the governing body and whether he chooses to continue representing Argentina after a World Cup campaign that ended in both defeat and controversy.
Article Summary: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes faces multiple assault charges following final defeat to Spain. 32-year-old has been charged with three counts of assault after Argentina's 1-0 extra-time defeat. If found guilty, he could theoretically receive a suspension totalling nine international matches, although reports have suggested a five or six-match ban is more likely.

Article Title: Postman becomes 'first Englishman to hold a World Cup winner's medal in 60 years' thanks to Marc Cucurella
Article Text:
Marc Cucurella let his local postman hold and wear Spain’s World Cup winner’s medal during a routine mail delivery, leaving fans praising the Real Madrid defender’s humble gesture.

A memorable delivery for one lucky postman

Daily Mail

Fans praise the defender's humility

Horsham became home for Cucurella and his family

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New chapter begins at Real Madrid

Marc Cucurella may have completed one of the biggest transfers of the summer after joining Real Madrid, but it is a simple act of kindness away from the pitch that has caught the attention of football fans.The Spain defender, who helped his country lift the 2026 FIFA World Cup last month, was praised after allowing his local postman to hold and even wear his winner's medal while delivering mail to the footballer's home in Horsham, West Sussex.The wholesome interaction quickly spread across social media, with supporters applauding the defender's down-to-earth nature despite having just reached the pinnacle of international football.The story emerged after local postman Gary shared his experience on a Horsham community social media page. According to the, Gary had stopped by Cucurella's home during one of his final delivery rounds when the Spain international struck up a conversation with him.The exchange soon became an unforgettable one.Gary revealed that Cucurella allowed him to hold, and even wear, the gold medal Spain won after defeating Argentina in the World Cup final in the United States last month."Had the pleasure of chatting to local World Cup winner Marc Cucurella while delivering his post today. Very nice, down-to-earth guy. Let me hold his winners' medal." Gary said.Reflecting on the encounter, he joked that he believed he was "the first Englishman to hold a World Cup winner's medal in 60 years,"The post prompted a wave of appreciative reactions online, with supporters celebrating the simple act of kindness.One fan commented: "The biggest and greatest accolade for any football player. And he was kind enough to share that."Another wrote: "Amazing stuff. He sounds like a really nice guy."A long-time follower of the Horsham community page added: "Amazing. We keep hearing great things and sorry to be losing him. Wishing him the best of luck in his new adventures."The photographs shared alongside the post also attracted attention, showing Cucurella sporting a newly braided hairstyle—a noticeable departure from the distinctive curly locks that have become one of his trademarks.The new look is one of several changes following Spain's World Cup triumph, with the left-back also making good on a promise he made during the tournament by getting a tattoo of head coach Luis de la Fuente's face to commemorate the historic victory.Cucurella has lived in Horsham since arriving in England, having moved there after a burglary at a previous property following his transfer to Chelsea in 2023.The market town became a quiet base for the defender and his family, who integrated into the local community. They reportedly became familiar faces at their children's schools and were regular visitors to local businesses, including an Indian restaurant in the area.His partner, Claudia Rodríguez, admitted after his move to Real Madrid that leaving England would not be easy. In an emotional social media message, she described Horsham as their home, thanked friends and Chelsea supporters for their support over the years, and reflected on raising their children during the family's time in England.Her comments contrasted sharply with the difficult period the family experienced following the earlier burglary, when she had previously spoken publicly about concerns over their safety and the emotional impact it had on their family life.Cucurella has now returned to Spain after completing his $64 million (€55 million) transfer from Chelsea to Real Madrid, with the deal officially finalised and announced on June 15, 2026. The 28-year-old arrives at the Santiago Bernabéu fresh from helping Spain win the 2026 FIFA World Cup and has signed a six-year contract that will keep him at the club until June 2032.He is set to play under José Mourinho, who returned to Real Madrid ahead of the 2026-27 season and identified the Spanish left-back as a priority addition to reinforce his defence. With pre-season preparations now under way, Cucurella will look to quickly establish himself in Mourinho's plans as Madrid begin their pursuit of La Liga, the UEFA Champions League and other major honours in the new campaign.
Article Summary: Marc Cucurella let his local postman hold and wear Spain's World Cup winner’s medal during a routine mail delivery. Fans praise the Real Madrid defender's humble gesture. The story emerged after postman Gary shared his experience on a Horsham community social media page.
